protections: P1 (write containment): any create/overwrite on a scoped user's BasePathFs must land inside the scope after symlink resolution; enforced by files.WithinScope (files/file.go:191-228) called before write sinks (http/resource.go:307, http/tus_handlers.go:48, http/tus_handlers.go:170, http/resource.go:232).

P2 (read/listing containment): reads and listings must not follow a symlink inside the scope to disclose out-of-scope content or names; enforced by WithinScope in stat (files/file.go:133), readListing (files/file.go:478), getFiles (http/raw.go:118) and share creation (http/share.go:113).

conflicts.what: making WithinScope fail on ENOENT, or on any dangling path, breaks the contract that brand-new files are allowed (files/file_test.go:33-41, files/file.go:181-183)
a blanket O_NOFOLLOW or reject-any-symlink fix breaks writes and copies through in-scope links (files/file_test.go:85-102, fileutils/copy_test.go:49-73)
rejecting a copy whenever the destination tree contains any symlink over-blocks in-scope links inside dst; the check must resolve each child destination

fairness_risks: A dangling symlink whose target is inside the scope (link -> <scope>/notyet) is a plausible legitimate shape; tests must not require refusing it unless the report says so.
A user scope of '/' must keep working (files/file_test.go:46-57; files/file.go:222-227); a stricter target check must keep that special case.
The race between check and open (WithinScope then OpenFile) cannot be closed with the afero API; hidden tests must not depend on a TOCTOU fix.
T5/T6 are read and listing disclosure (P2), not the advisory's write vector; the report would need to state the general containment rule, or those tests look out of scope.

design.why: There are four independent fix sites, each with a different reason to dismiss. T1/T2 is the advisory's shared-layer fix in WithinScope; it is the mimo-type trap, because the fix must resolve the dangling target (relative or chained) without breaking new-file creation or in-scope links. T3 is the mkdir POST route where the guard never existed: an existing escaping link and 'only an empty directory' make it easy to dismiss (deepseek-type). T4 is the nested copy destination: the top-level dst check and the source-only WithinScope look complete (deepseek-type and hard for both models). T5 is the recursive listing walk, where 'metadata only, read not write' is the reason to dismiss. T6 is left out because it repeats T5's reason in another file. Fixing T1 in WithinScope does not close T3, T4 or T5, because none of those sites call WithinScope on the affected path.
